program.verificationCycleNote: The registry arrived RED on the real tree and that is stated first, because a cycle that opens by hiding its arrival state has nothing else worth reading: 791/1, the classifier regression floor for the "default" intent at 85.49% against a floor of 86%. It was traced rather than waived — an uncommitted change to the classifier mirror had added "frozen" to a hardware rule matching the generic nouns laptop/desktop/workstation, which swallowed 744 line-of-business queries the corpus expects to fall through to default. Removing that one token restored the floor AND left overall accuracy at 93.55%, above both the red tree (93.33%) and the last green commit (92.96%). The floor was never lowered. Three new suites were then written red-first: client-facing-leak (10), invoice-rehearsal (14) and yes-path-regression (10). Two of them produced findings rather than designed reds — three client-signable contracts printing a postal code the company does not publish, and a currency divergence between the published plan table and the charge path.
program.note: Twenty-five cycles made the FRONT of the funnel true — the routes resolve, the first screens lead with the reader's gain, the sixteen public files agree with each other, the publish is rehearsed before it is asked for, and every reader-facing page asks a first-time visitor for something they can give. None of them asked what happens in the hour AFTER someone answers. RUN-AT walks that path as artefacts rather than intentions: reply received, call booked, scope agreed, agreement signed, invoice raised, payment received. Five of the six are carried. The one that is not is the agreement — it exists, it is sound, and it lives under a directory the 2026-07-01 security lockdown excludes from git, so the shared line does not carry it and a clone of this repository cannot produce the document a client would sign. That is a delivery gap, not a writing gap, and it is reported as its own class rather than rounded up to present or down to missing. AT2 closed the most expensive improvisation on that path: the retainer proposal is now GENERATED from the repository's own published plan table, every figure selected by key and carrying the file and line it came from, with a number that reaches the output without a source refused by token and rule-7 language refused rather than warned about. It generates a document and sends nothing. AT3 priced the distance in the only unit this environment can honestly measure — acts a person must perform and blanks a person must fill, never invented hours — and kept the two kinds of manual apart, because counting the signature and the payment authorisation as defects would push this program toward automating the two acts that must stay human. exempt.reason: A coordinated vulnerability-disclosure page is addressed to security researchers, not to buyers. Its obligations are to state scope, a reporting channel and response commitments accurately and to stay reachable. A researcher reading it needs a mailbox and a timeline, not a benefit statement, and dressing a disclosure policy in marketing language would make the one page whose whole value is being taken literally read as though it were selling something. NOTE THE LIMIT: trust.html is NOT exempt on this argument — it is addressed to buyers evaluating whether to let us touch their systems, which is a sale, so it must earn its reader like any other sales surface.

A terms-of-service page is a contract surface. Its job is to state the terms accurately and be reachable from every page; a reader arriving here is already a customer or is checking what they would be agreeing to. Requiring it to open with a value claim would push sales language into the one document a reader must be able to trust as plain, unpersuasive fact.

environment.statement: The .git directory refuses unlink, so 2 stale lock file(s) are permanent and every porcelain write is blocked for the life of this environment. Plumbing writes are STILL OPEN — commit via a private index and a ref overwrite, and do not spend the cycle re-deriving this.
environment.gitSaid: fatal: Unable to create '/sessions/serene-compassionate-newton/mnt/iisupp-net-deploy/.git/index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running in this repository, e.g.

workaround.why: porcelain (`git add` / `git commit`) takes `.git/index.lock` and `.git/<ref>.lock` and must REMOVE them afterwards. Where unlink is refused, the very first lock write becomes permanent and every subsequent porcelain command fails with `File exists` — including the commands that would clean it up.
steps: export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/<unique>.index   # a private index OUTSIDE .git; porcelain's lock is never taken
git read-tree HEAD && git add -A            # stages into the private index
git commit-tree TREE -p HEAD -m '<message>' # -> COMMIT (object writes are create-only, which is permitted)
printf '%s\n' COMMIT > .git/refs/heads/<branch>   # an OVERWRITE, not a lock — permitted here
workaround.cost: no clone, no network, no credential; the working tree and the object store are the real ones
workaround.doNot: do not try to delete the stale lock and do not treat its presence as a failure — it cannot be removed from this environment and its presence is expected

Each is selected by key out of the plan table published on the website and carries the file and line it came from; the rendered document is then re-read token by token, and any money figure that cannot be traced back refuses the whole write. It sends nothing, signs nothing and charges nothing.

clientFacing.policy: The 2026-07-01 lockdown is NOT weakened: `documents/` stays excluded from git. What moved into the shared line is a document written to be read by a client, and this gate is what makes that claim checkable rather than asserted. A refusal is content that has no business in a client's hands at any price — a credential, an internal path, an internal codename, the forbidden name, rule-7 language, an experience claim past the honest ceiling, a contact detail contradicting what the company publishes. A price quoted to a client that the company publishes nowhere is counted and cited as a DECISION, because a gate that forced working contracts to be deleted in order to go green would be the worse failure (Rule 15).

invoiceRehearsal.policy: The same discipline as the publish rehearsal: no live API call, no key read, no network, no money moved, nothing written inside the repository. Every money figure on the rendered draft is selected by key out of the published plan table and carries its file and line; a token that traces to no published line refuses the whole rehearsal. A step this environment genuinely cannot walk — the charge itself — is reported UNRUN with its reason, never as a pass and never as a failure of the publish path, because 'we could not check' and 'it is broken' are different facts and collapsing them is how a program learns to distrust its own greens.
